C0002 has a strong single-pathway RNA identity (EMT, SMD=1.495, q=0.00155) with a large effect size and FDR support. WXS and CNV are not significant, but the RNA signal is coherent and not contradicted by other modalities. Technical factors are not significantly enriched at set level. Structural evidence shows weak cohesion, but no positive evidence supports Split or Merge. The EMT signal provides sufficient positive identity evidence to retain this candidate for downstream validation.

The top RNA pathway (mitotic spindle) is not significant (q=0.191), and WXS/CNV show only nominal trends with wide confidence intervals. There is no coherent biological identity to support retention. Structural evidence shows moderate internal structure but no modality provides a strong defining signal. Measured technical factors are not significantly enriched, but the absence of positive identity evidence makes Drop better supported than Accept, Split, or Merge.

WXS shows a nominal PBRM1 enrichment but not significant after correction. The RNA and CNV signals are consistent and biologically interpretable. Structural evidence shows moderate cross-modal consistency with positive WSI and RNA silhouettes and high patient support. Technical factors are not significantly enriched at set level. No positive evidence supports Split or Merge. Retaining C0004 is better supported than Drop.

WXS and CNV are not significant, but the RNA signal is strong and biologically coherent. Technical factors are not significantly enriched at set level. Structural evidence shows weak to moderate cohesion, but no positive evidence supports Split or Merge. The RNA signal provides sufficient positive identity evidence to retain this candidate.

C0006 has a coherent RNA-defined biological identity with 8 significant pathways, including downregulation of myogenesis and upregulation of inflammatory pathways. WXS shows a strong BAP1 enrichment trend (OR=7.71, p=0.0033) that approaches but does not reach FDR significance (q=0.073). The RNA signal is strong and biologically coherent, and the BAP1 trend adds suggestive support. However, the set has a significant technical association with CJ tissue source site (q=0.049), which provides a substantial alternative explanation. Given the strong RNA identity and the fact that the technical association is not the primary driver of the RNA signal, retaining C0006 is better supported than Drop. No positive evidence supports Split or Merge.

More importantly, the set has multiple significant technical associations (tissue source site B8, BP, CZ; ct_phase NEPH; ct_manufacturer GE/SIEMENS; ct_scanner_model; ct_reconstruction_kernel; ct_slice_thickness), indicating that technical factors provide a substantial alternative explanation for any observed differences. The absence of positive biological identity and the strong technical confounding make Drop better supported than Accept, Split, or Merge.
